Running out of room faster than you expected?

Tractors, trailers, equipment, tools — it doesn't take long before valuable equipment starts sitting outside.

A 40×60 pole barn can give you serious covered space while keeping the layout open and flexible for the way you actually use your property.

At South Dixie Storage, we help customers throughout Florida and Georgia find a building size and layout that fits what they need today — while giving them room for tomorrow.

Thinking about adding covered storage to your property? Give us a call and let's talk about what you're trying to build.

#PoleBarn #StorageSolutions #SouthDixieStorage

One of the biggest mistakes we see landowners make before ordering a pole barn kit: not accounting for site drainage. You can have the best kit money can buy, and if water pools where your posts go, you're setting yourself up for rot and structural issues down the road. Before you finalize your building site, walk it after a heavy rain. Where does the water go? That one step saves a lot of headaches — and we always ask our customers about it before we plan a delivery.

#PoleBarnTips #BuildRight

Picture this: it's the middle of harvest season, you've got a piece of equipment down, and you're crawling around under it in the heat because you have nowhere covered to work. No shade, no shelter, no flat floor. A pole barn with a simple concrete apron and some overhead clearance completely changes that scenario — and it's one of the most practical upgrades a working farm can make. A workshop bay inside your storage building isn't a luxury, it's a tool.
